theme: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919: a sticky disaster that somehow brought people together.

events.text: Hey, you remember that CN Tower licence plate bit? I was reading about the Great Molasses Flood of 1919 and—
The what now? That sounds like a dessert gone rogue.
A giant tank of molasses burst in Boston. Sent a wave of syrup through the streets at like 35 miles an hour.
Thirty-five miles an hour? That's faster than the streetcar on Queen. And stickier.
People actually got trapped in it. It was two and a half million gallons of the stuff.
Okay, that's horrifying and also... I kind of want to see a wave of molasses. Is that wrong?
So I fell down a rabbit hole. The molasses was for making rum and munitions during World War I.
Rum and munitions? That's the most 1919 sentence I've ever heard.
And the tank was shoddily built. They painted it brown to hide the leaks.
Classic. If you can't fix it, paint it the colour of the thing that's leaking.
The court case took six years. It's still one of the longest in Massachusetts history.
Six years of lawyers arguing about syrup. I bet they all needed a double-double after that.
I'm just saying, if a molasses flood hit this No Thrills, we'd be stuck to the floor like flies on flypaper.
Don't give the universe ideas. We still have to get through the checkout.
Did somebody say molasses? I've got a cousin who swears the flood was caused by a secret society of pancake enthusiasts.
Kessler, that's not—
They meet on the third Tuesday. Very sticky business. I've said too much.
Every time. Every single time we come here.
You know what got me? After the flood, people came from all over to help clean up. Neighbours, strangers, even kids.
Really? In the middle of all that goo?
Yeah. It was a disaster, but it also brought the city together. Like a really gross, sticky block party.
That's weirdly beautiful. Like us, but with more molasses.
I even found a souvenir licence plate from the 75th anniversary. It says 'Molasses Flood Survivor'.
Of course you did. Put it next to the CN Tower one. Our wall is becoming a museum of weird Toronto-adjacent history.
And you're the only person I'd want to be stuck in a molasses wave with.
Same. But if it happens, I'm holding your hand so we don't drift apart. Literally.
